⚖️ PROPERTY LAW | BIHAR LAND DISPUTES
Does Mutation (Dakhil-Kharij) Make You the Legal Owner of a Property?
This is one of the most common misconceptions in land and property matters.
Many people believe that once their name appears in the Jamabandi or revenue records, their ownership over the land is legally established.
But the legal position is more nuanced.
In Tarachandra v. Bhawarlal & Anr., Civil Appeal No. 15077 of 2025, decided on 19 December 2025, the Supreme Court of India reiterated an important principle:
Mutation entries in revenue records do not, by themselves, create or confer ownership rights or title over a property.
The primary purpose of mutation is fiscal — it enables the revenue authorities to identify the person responsible for payment of land revenue.
The Court also clarified an important aspect concerning mutation applications based on a Will: such applications cannot be rejected merely because the claim is based on a Will, where the applicable law permits it and the claim is undisputed.
Why is this important in Bihar?
In Bihar, property-related disputes frequently involve:
• Disputes over Khata and Khesra numbers.
• Cancellation of old Jamabandi.
• Mutation in the name of legal heirs.
• Competing claims based on registered sale deeds and inheritance.
• Disputes concerning possession and ownership.
• Objections raised during mutation proceedings.
A revenue entry, a registered sale deed and a judicial declaration of title serve different legal purposes. They should not be treated as interchangeable documents.
A Legal Perspective
One must distinguish between three important questions:
Who is recorded in the revenue records?
Who is in actual possession of the property?
Who has legally established title over the property?
These questions may overlap, but they are not necessarily the same.
A complicated dispute concerning ownership cannot ordinarily be conclusively determined merely through mutation proceedings. The appropriate legal remedy depends on the nature of the dispute, applicable revenue law and available evidence.
The fundamental principle is clear: Revenue records are important, but ownership must be established in accordance with law.
Understanding this distinction is essential before purchasing property, inheriting land or challenging a mutation entry.
Adv. Smriti Tiwari
Advocate, Patna High Court
